 Judgment
This is an appeal filed by the claimant aggrieved by the award passed in MVC.No.979/2011 dated 31.05.2012 on the file of the Presiding Officer, FTC-III & MACT, Mysore.
The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.9,35,000/- with interest at 12% per annum for the injuries sustained by the claimant in the accident that occurred on 06.01.2011.

The case of the claimant is that he is aged about 25 years, working as a mason earning an amount of Rs.10,000/-, while he was moving on his TVS XL moped at about 11.00 a.m. on 06.01.2011 from JP nagar to link road, at that time a car came in the opposite direction dashed the claimant, he fell down and sustained injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to the B.G.S Apollo Hospital and then shifted to K.R. Hospital, Mysore, wherein he was inpatient for a period of 96 days.

The insurance company filed the written statement denying name, age, address, occupation,
monthly income of claimant, nature of accident and injuries sustained by the claimant and they also contended that the accident occurred only due to the negligence on the part of the claimant, hence the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

On the ground of liability, the court below held that as the NC: 2023:KHC:33809 claimant was not having valid driving license, inspite of giving an opportunity, he had failed to produce the same, he had taken the stand that he had lost the Driving License.
The court gave a finding that he ought to have applied for the duplicate and he should have submitted before the court.

In the process of giving such a finding, the court had disbelieved the evidence of the claimant, however it had come to the conclusion that in the way, that Kumara vs Smt Radha on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194997422/
2 his evidence is not trustworthy and it is doubtful as to whether the claimant knew driving of the two wheeler and had an effective and valid driving license.

sentences.text:
Therefore in the absence of driving license,
the court held that the accident occurred due to the contributory negligence on the part of the claimant and apportioned the same at 25% on the claimant and 75% on the driver of the offending vehicle.

Then coming to the compensation, the court under the head of pain and suffering granted an amount of Rs.35,000/-, towards the medical expenditure and as per the evidence on record granted an amount of Rs.1,34,600/-, when it comes to loss of income during the NC:
2023:KHC:33809 laid up period

, the court below had granted an amount of Rs.12,000/-, towards attendant charges granted an amount of Rs.9,600/-, towards special diet granted an amount of Rs.9,600/-, towards loss of amenities granted an amount of Rs.50,000/-.
As it is case of the claimant that he had sustained the disability, there is shortening of leg by one inch but he had failed to examine the doctor who had treated him.

The court had granted only an amount of Rs.50,000/-
towards loss of amenities without applying the multiplier.
Towards future medical expenses an amount of Rs.20,000/- was granted, altogether granted an amount of Rs.2,75,800/-.
The contributory negligence was assessed at 25%, the claim peititon was allowed directing the insurance company to pay an amount of Rs.2,03,100/-.
Aggrieved by the award passed thereby, the claimant is before this court.
3. Learned counsel for the claimant submits that the court below without any basis had assessed the contributory negligence.
It is submitted that just because NC: 2023:KHC:33809 the driver was not having a driving license, that itself cannot be a ground for the court to fix the contributory negligence.
It is submitted that for the injuries sustained by the claimant, the amounts that were awarded by the Tribunal were not reasonable.

He submits that when he was there for 96 days in the hospital, towards loss of income during the treatment period, only an amount of Rs.12,000/- was granted by the Tribunal which is on the lower side and it is not a reasonable compensation.

4. Sri B. Pradeep, Learned Counsel for the insurance company submits that court below had rightly considered the evidence of the claimant and held that there is 25% contributory negligence on the part of the claimant.
It is submitted that when there was no evidence, the court below had taken Rs.3,000/- as the income and rightly granted an amount of Rs.12,000/- towards loss of income during treatment period.
He submits that burden lies on the claimant to prove that he sustained disability by adducing the evidence and he failed NC: 2023:KHC:33809 to adduce the evidence.
It is submitted that the court below was right in not granting any amount towards disability.

It is submitted that the compensation that was granted was just and reasonable and no grounds are made out seeking enhancement of the compensation, as the respondent failed to prove that there is contributory negligence on the part of the claimant.
5.
Having heard the Counsels on either side, perused the entire material on record.
When it comes to contributory negligence, just because the claimant was not having valid driving license, that itself is not a ground for the court below to fix the contributory negligence.
The contention of the learned counsel for the insurance company is that the looking at the manner in which the accident had happened, the court has given such a finding.

Such submission this court is not able to appreciate for the reason that the court has given a specific finding for fixing the contributory negligence is that the claimant was not having driving license.

Such finding of the court below is NC:

3 2023:KHC:33809 without any basis and the same is set aside and the entire negligence is fixed on the driver of the offending vehicle.
